title: Observability-led throughput harness notes and variance-mitigation checklist
content:
Purpose
This doc captures an observability-first approach to running throughput benchmarks for the serving runtime. Aim: make runs repeatable and actionable by tying loadgen configs to a small set of cross-layer signals so we can explain outliers quickly (instead of re-running 20 times).

Audience
- Runtime engineers doing perf investigations
- QA/benchmarking engineers validating commits
- SREs helping interpret noisy runs

High-level approach (one-sentence)
Bind load patterns to an observability checklist: baseline metrics, hardware counters, scheduler state, and deterministic priming. If a metric drifts, the checklist points to which layer to re-run with tighter controls.

Why different from previous notes
- Prior docs emphasize RNG seeds, priming windows and arrival distributions. This doc organizes experiments around signals (e.g., GPU SM occupancy, kernel stalls, NVLink traffic, scheduler preemption) and prescribes targeted mitigations.
- Goal is faster triage: given a bad-variance run we want to know which control to flip next.

Core signals to capture for every run (minimum set)
1) Client-level: request rate, p95/p99 latency, backlog length, concurrency histogram
2) Serving runtime: queue depths (per-worker), dispatch latency (enqueue->start), kv-cache hit ratio, batch sizes distribution
3) GPU-level: SM occupancy, compute utilization, memory bandwidth (GB/s), PCIe/NVLink throughput, GPU temperature, GPU clock throttles
4) OS-level: CPU steal, runqueue length per CPU, context-switch rate, irq/softirq load
5) Kernel/driver: GPU driver stalls (nvidia-smi dmon/dmesg samples), cupti API counters if available
6) Network (if cross-host): socket retransmits, kernel tx queue drops, NIC driver ring occupancy

Minimum tracing hooks to enable per-benchmark run
- RT tracepoints: request_id -> enqueue_ts -> dispatch_ts -> start_kernel_ts -> token_emit_ts
- Annotate traces with model.* metadata (quantization level, kv_cache_enabled, batch_policy)
- Export spans to tracing backend with same run-id tag (helps correlate with GPU traces)

Standard run metadata
- run_id: RFC3339 timestamp + short git sha (e.g., 2024-10-03T15:22:12Z-g3f1a2c)
- model: model name / variant / quantization
- batch_policy: continuous|micro|fixed-N
- sequence_length_p95
- priming_sequence: brief description (e.g., single 128-token priming, 40 requests)
- load_profile_name: e.g., steady-500rps, poisson-burst-1000-10s, microburst-200x10ms

Loadgen config suggestions (examples)
- steady-100rps: fixed inter-arrival for 30m, concurrency cap 200, warmup 10m (target median latency < SLO).
- poisson-1000-burst10s: target mean 1000 rps, burst windows of 10s every 2m (seeded RNG=1234), warmup 20m including several burst cycles.
- microburst-stress-200x10ms: emulate client bursts: 200 concurrent arrivals every 10ms for 5s, repeat 30 times with 30s cool-off. Useful for slot/slot-queue starvation profiling.

Warmup and priming heuristics (observability-led)
- Two-phase warmup: 1) traffic priming to fill kv-cache (if enabled) - send N distinct prompts designed to exercise tokens that exercise long KV lifetimes (N depends on model; use small synthesized corpus). 2) steady-state ramp: ramp to target load over 10-20 minutes with sample traces collected throughout.
- Always capture first-5-min and last-5-min of warmup separately. Look for decreasing tail latencies and increasing cache hit ratio. If those metrics plateau early, shorter warmup ok.
- Priming seed convention: use deterministic content (git-controlled prompt corpus) and note corpus version in run metadata.

Repeatability controls (checklist)
- Machine-level: BIOS power management -> performance mode on; disable turbo if testing thermal stability; pin CPU governors to performance.
- Affinity: set CPU/GPU affinity and document (taskset/numactl). Note NUMA region used for GPU DMA.
- Isolate benchmark host from noisy background workloads: cgroups to limit unrelated processes, isolate cpus with isolcpus.
- Kernel: use consistent kernel version across runs; disable transparent hugepages for experiments that observe large variance.
- GPU drivers: use driver build X (record nvidia-smi --query), capture dmesg pre/post run.
- Loadgen: deterministic RNG for arrival times when using synthetic jitter; record seed in run metadata.

Variance diagnostic flow (when run is noisy)
1) Check queueing signals: is queue depth oscillating? If yes, inspect batch size distribution and latency tails.
2) Check GPU utilization pattern: spikes with low SM occupancy + high GPU memory bandwidth hints at memory-bound kernels or thrashing.
3) If host CPU is high on irq/softirq, suspect networking or driver interrupts—capture tcpdump and NIC counters.
4) If many context-switches/runqueue pressure, investigate cgroup/cpu affinity and other processes.
5) Correlate GPU temperature/clocks with dips in throughput => thermal throttling.
6) If every run shows high variance only at specific payload sizes, instrument kernel selection path and compare kernel map between runs.

Examples of targeted mitigations (mapping signal->control)
- NVLink/PCIe congestion: pin network/host processes away from DMA CPUs; increase PCIe write coalescing; reduce cross-host shard traffic.
- KV-cache churn: increase cache TTL or use pre-warm sequences; lower batch sizes to reduce eviction pressure.
- Scheduler preemption: raise SCHED_FIFO weight for infer threads in canary runs or isolate CPUs.
- Kernel selection nondeterminism: pin thread to single core, fix thread pool sizing to reduce contention for compilation/one-time setup paths.

Quick triage checklist (to run immediately after noisy failure)
- Collect run_id and attach traces + nvidia-smi CSV for the run window
- Copy kernel dmesg and driver logs
- Export OS perf top/samples for high CPU threads
- Dump model weights checksum and quantization tag
- Re-run a short deterministic micro-run (single-sequence, fixed seed, low concurrency) to test base correctness

Experiment templates (short reproducible plays)
- Micro-run: single-sequence 128 tokens, seed=42, concurrency=1, 30s run. Goal: verify identical token outputs and a stable small-latency baseline.
- Cache-priming validation: run priming corpus v3 then measure cache hit ratio over next 1k requests vs no-priming.
- Thread-affinity A/B: same run with taskset vs default, collect run-level metrics and compare p95/p99.

Unresolved questions / TODOs
- How to capture CUpti counters reliably across large fleets? Prereqs and overhead need measurement.
- Is there a standardized minimal priming corpus we can commit in infra repo? Draft exists in bench-harness PR 842 but needs review.
- Should we record GPU PMU counters at 1s resolution by default? Storage cost vs insight tradeoff.

Notes to self (quick reminders)
- Add a small script to synthesize priming corpus given model tokenizer (avoid manual steps).
- Add a run-id mapping table into the bench S3 bucket for quick lookup.
- When flaky runs are observed, reduce window to isolate microburst occurrences rather than long 30m windows.

References and helpful commands
- nvidia-smi dmon mode (watch mem and sm utilization)
- cupti sampling APIs (link internal PR)
- perf record --call-graph for hot threads (cpu-side)
- tcpdump -i any -w run_{run_id}.pcap (for cross-host traffic diagnosis)

Appendix: minimal run template (copyable)
- run metadata: run_id, git_sha, model, batch_policy, priming_corpus_version, seed
- loadgen cli: --profile steady-100rps --seed 1234 --warmup-min 20 --concurrency-cap 200 --trace true
- observability: enable-traces=true, gpu-metrics-interval=5s, export-to=tracing-backend:bench-runs

End notes
This is a living note. The emphasis here is on coupling bench configs with the right telemetry so triage is faster. I expect to convert the most common checklist items into automated preflight validators in bench-harness (PR 842 is a start).
